 Sony launches MDR-3R retro wired headphones inspired by original Walkman-era design
 The new product is retailing at between £49.99 and £59.99 across two colourways
 Sony has launched a new set of wired headphones inspired by its original Walkman-era design from 1979.
 The MDR-3R on-ear headphones are available in two colourways: a classic silver finish and a Stranger Things -themed edition. The standard model is priced at £49.99, while the special edition retails at £59.99. Both versions quickly sold out on Sony’s website following the launch yesterday (5th November), with further availability yet to be confirmed.
 The lightweight headphones come with interchangeable blue and orange earpads, allowing users to switch between the two colours. They can also be connected directly to a phone, tablet or PC via USB-C, offering instant music playback, built-in playback controls and hands-free calling, with no charging or Bluetooth pairing required.
 Sony says the new model has been designed to retain the character of its original 1979 MDR-3L2 headphones, while introducing updates to improve audio performance. The company describes the sound as well-balanced, with deeper bass, more extended highs and greater vocal clarity.
 Check out the headphones  here .
 The Sony MDR-3, which the new headphones are based on, were introduced alongside the first Walkman, the TPS-L2, and became an iconic part of Sony’s early portable audio range.
 The decision to update the original design comes amid a surge in the use of wired earphones and headphones for normal audio listening in recent years as some people have shifted away from wireless products. In September, Bose launched its first new set of wired earbuds in 11 years .
 The Prodigy also unveiled a new wired set of earphones as part of their BLK.ANT creative project last month.
 In the wireless market, AlphaTheta recently unveiled a new pair of wireless DJ headphones, the HDJ-F9 .
